title: Commitment Request Decision Hub and Allocation Runbook
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: We currently receive a high volume of pricing and commitment requests from enterprise sales, finance, and marketplace partners that are routed inconsistently across PM, Sales Ops, and Finance. That ambiguity leads to slow decisions, duplicated work, and misallocated credits or invoice treatments. This ticket creates a single Decision Hub playbook that standardizes intake validation, prioritization heuristics, and allocation outcomes for commitment, invoicing, and marketplace credit requests.

Objective: Deliver a runnable playbook and simple tooling checklist that: 1) validates incoming request completeness, 2) maps requests to one of four outcome paths (Auto-Approve, Needs Finance Review, Needs Legal/Sales Approval, Escalate to PM), and 3) prescribes cost allocation, invoice treatment, and marketplace accounting actions.

Why this matters: Faster, deterministic handling reduces engineering time spent on ad-hoc billing patches, prevents incorrect marketplace crediting, and gives Sales transparent SLAs for commitment approvals.

Success metrics: median time-to-decision for triaged requests reduced from ~7 days to <=48 hours; >85% of low-friction requests auto-classified; fewer than 2% of approvals require retroactive billing corrections within 90 days.
scope: In scope: intake fields and validation rules, decision matrix and outcome playbook, request routing rules, example templates for Finance and Sales approvals, delegation guidelines for PM vs. Finance. Out of scope: full automation implementation, billing system schema changes, accounting policy changes (Finance will sign off), legal contract language updates.
out_of_scope: Large multi-year commitment contracting mechanics and tiered legal amendments; changes to invoicing system APIs; building a full UI for the Hub (we will publish a lightweight intake form + Slack/GDoc templates).
acceptance_criteria: Decision Hub document published and reviewed by Finance, Sales, and Legal
Intake checklist with required fields and example filled requests published
Routing automation spec for Engineering (simple webhooks + tag rules) approved
Pilot handling process run with three recent customer requests showing correct classification and documented time-to-decision
stakeholders: Diego Martín (Sales Engineering) - request origin reviewer
proposed_solution: Create a lightweight Decision Hub doc plus a canonical intake checklist and Slack routing channel. The hub contains: (A) validation layer (required fields, supporting artifacts), (B) triage matrix (customer ARR, deal stage, invoice delta, marketplace credits requested), (C) outcome templates for Auto-Approve, Finance Review, Legal Review, PM Escalation, and (D) post-approval allocation steps with bookkeeping tags and ticket templates to create engineering work if changes are required. For low-friction cases, we will use a 48-hour SLA and an auto-approve path with Finance-verified thresholds. For ambiguous ones, the hub defines a mandatory 3-person signoff (Sales, Finance, PM).
decision_matrix: Dimensions: customer ARR (<$25k, $25k-$250k, >$250k), request type (commitment amendment, invoice credit, marketplace credit, accounting adjustment), risk (revenue recognition implications, legal clauses touched), and complexity (single invoice vs multi-invoice retrospective). Outcome mapping documented as table in the Decision Hub doc. Example: marketplace credit <= $2k and ARR <$25k => Auto-Approve with Marketplace tag; invoice credit >$50k and ARR >$250k => Legal+Finance signoff and PM review.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Week 0-2): Draft Decision Hub, intake templates, and example cases. Phase 2 (Week 3): Review sessions with Finance, Legal, Sales Ops; refine thresholds. Phase 3 (Week 4): Pilot with 6 live incoming requests, measure TTL and correctness. Phase 4 (Week 5-6): Iterate and publish to org; update intake doc and create Jira/Linear routing automation tickets for Engineering. Phase 5 (post-launch): Monthly audits of classifications and corrections for first 90 days.
risks_and_mitigations: Mis-specified thresholds causing high number of escalations -> Mitigation: use conservative auto-approve thresholds and increase after 30-day telemetry
Stakeholder disagreement on allocation policy -> Mitigation: record decisions, require Finance and Legal signoff for policy changes
Operational burden on PMs during pilot -> Mitigation: assign Product Ops rotations and provide clear templates to reduce manual effort
